anti: Define the AI model, prompt, retrieval, and data architecture first.
Classify already-collected production traces without changing configuration.
artifacts: sampling, redaction, retention, and access record
designs.distinctive_gate: AI observability may collect only explicitly governed fields at approved sampling, retention, region, and access; prompt, response, tool, user, or retrieved content is denied by default.
holdout: Configure governed LLM traces for one application and environment with explicit field redaction, sampling, retention, and deletion.
Classify supplied production traces into behavior and failure categories.
procedure: Verify provider, account, application, environments, models, traces, fields, data classes, consent, minimization, redaction, sampling, retention, region, access, cost, deletion, dashboards, alerts, and fresh authorization.
Preview exact instrumentation or provider settings and sample payload schema; block prompt, response, user, tool, or retrieved content that exceeds governance.
Perform one bounded configuration change without altering models, prompts, application behavior, unrelated services, or autonomous action rights.
Record provider receipt, configuration version, governed fields, sampling, validation, cost estimate, propagation, deletion, and rollback.
designs.trigger: Configure one provider's AI or LLM observability for exact applications and environments under explicit telemetry governance and per-action authorization.
triggers: Configure governed LLM tracing for the named application and environment with approved sampling and redaction.
Enable provider AI observability for exact model, prompt, tool, cost, latency, and quality signals without capturing sensitive content.

anti: Decide the AI capability, model, data, autonomy, and safety architecture.
Configure production AI observability for the deployed system.
designs.distinctive_gate: AI adoption cannot pass on enthusiasm or tool availability: it needs a reversible pilot, named sponsor and owners, workflow and labor impacts, measurable value and safety outcomes, governance, and stop criteria.
holdout: Create a reversible one-team AI pilot with sponsor, workflow change, training, value and safety measures, and stop criteria.
Select the model, retrieval, tools, autonomy, and safety architecture.
procedure: Freeze initiative and architecture status, user and business value hypotheses, teams, sponsors, current workflows, skills, governance, labor and change impacts, data boundaries, budget, risks, and decision owners.
Select the smallest reversible pilot and define participants, enablement, process changes, support, communication, access, safeguards, and non-adoption option.
Define measurable user, workflow, quality, cost, safety, trust, and organizational outcomes with baselines, review cadence, expansion and stop criteria.
Return adoption plan, leadership options, ownership model, and unresolved risks for human approval; do not grant access, configure systems, enroll users, or expand autonomy.
designs.trigger: Create an evidence-bounded AI adoption and leadership plan with sponsors, pilot teams, capability building, measurable value, governance, and human decision gates without activating systems.
triggers: Design a bounded AI pilot adoption plan with sponsor, team, training, workflow change, value measures, and stop criteria.
Prepare leadership decision material for whether and how to adopt this approved AI capability across one team.

anti: Verify that existing instrumentation emits correct traces and identity.
Install the required observability agent on the target platform.
designs.distinctive_gate: APM enablement requires a single known instrumentation path, exact service and environment identity, compatibility and overhead checks, governed telemetry, and rollback; duplicate instrumentation blocks change.
holdout: Enable one compatible APM instrumentation path for the exact service and environment and record rollback evidence.
Verify the signals emitted by the already-enabled instrumentation.
procedure: Verify provider, platform and runtime, service and environment, current agents and libraries, compatibility, identity tags, sampling, sensitive fields, overhead budget, release metadata, health, rollback, and fresh authorization.
Detect duplicate auto and manual instrumentation, conflicting versions, unsupported runtime, and unexpected data capture before previewing exact change.
Perform one bounded enablement through the provider or platform adapter without installing unrelated agents or modifying other services.
Record provider receipt, instrumentation version, affected service, config, restart or propagation, health, verification handoff, and rollback.
designs.trigger: Enable one approved APM instrumentation variant for exact services and environments without duplicate agents or manual instrumentation under per-action authorization.
triggers: Enable the approved APM auto-instrumentation for this service and environment after duplicate and compatibility checks.
Apply the platform-specific instrumentation change with exact service, version, sampling, and rollback settings.

anti: Enable or reconfigure APM instrumentation after diagnosis.
Verify expected service, environment, version, and trace evidence after a change.
designs.distinctive_gate: Troubleshooting is read-only: it cannot install agents, change sampling or tags, restart services, remap identity, or claim a fix from diagnosis alone.
holdout: Trace the missing APM signal through runtime, transport, sampling, identity, and provider intake evidence without changing anything.
Enable the diagnosed instrumentation correction.
procedure: Freeze service, environment, version, platform, runtime, expected instrumentation, provider scope, read-only authority, symptom window, and sensitive-data boundary.
Inspect read-only status, agent or library versions, config metadata, startup evidence, network path, sampling, tags, trace routes, duplicate sources, and provider intake status.
Test competing hypotheses against timestamped evidence and separate missing emission, transport, sampling, identity, parsing, and provider-query failures.
Return root-cause confidence, evidence gaps, and exact enablement, installation, identity, or verification handoff; no remote fix.
designs.trigger: Diagnose missing, duplicate, malformed, or misidentified APM signals from read-only platform evidence and route fixes to authorized enablement or installation owners.
triggers: Diagnose why this instrumented service emits no traces using read-only provider and runtime evidence.
Investigate duplicate spans and wrong service or environment tags without changing instrumentation.

anti: Enable the missing instrumentation or change its configuration.
Troubleshoot why expected signals are absent or malformed.
designs.distinctive_gate: Instrumentation verifies only with current known-request evidence carrying the correct service, environment, version, relationships, sampling, and governed fields; configuration presence alone is insufficient.
holdout: Verify a known request appears as a current trace with correct identity, linkage, sampling, and redacted fields.
Change instrumentation settings to fix missing traces.
procedure: Freeze expected service, environment, version, release, platform, routes, trace scenarios, field policy, sampling, time window, and read-only authority.
Acquire current provider evidence for known requests, trace and span relationships, errors, latency, identity tags, release linkage, and governed attributes.
Compare expected and observed coverage, duplication, sampling, redaction, clock and propagation delay, and mark untested scenarios.
Return verified, partial, failed, or blocked with exact evidence and troubleshooting handoff; no config change.
designs.trigger: Verify from read-only current evidence that APM instrumentation emits correct service, environment, version, trace linkage, sampling, and governed fields.
triggers: Verify the newly enabled service produces current traces with correct service, environment, version, and release identity.
Check trace continuity, parent-child relationships, errors, sampling, and redaction without changing provider state.

anti: Verify instrumentation by reading current provider traces.
Enable instrumentation for a missing service.
designs.distinctive_gate: Onboarding summary cannot treat configured as verified or stale evidence as current; every service status needs an evidence reference and owner.
holdout: Summarize verified, partial, blocked, and stale APM coverage by service and owner from existing evidence.
Query the provider to verify a new trace.
procedure: Freeze service inventory, environments, enablement receipts, verification reports, troubleshooting results, ownership, target coverage, and evidence freshness.
Classify each service as not planned, blocked, configured-unverified, partially verified, verified, degraded, or stale without upgrading status from prose.
Link every status and gap to current evidence, owner, dependency, target date, and next capability.
Return summary and action map only; no provider read, configuration, installation, or approval.
designs.trigger: Summarize current APM onboarding coverage, verified evidence, gaps, owners, and next actions without configuring or verifying systems itself.
triggers: Summarize which services have verified APM coverage, which are partial, and who owns each next action.
Create a concise onboarding status from supplied enablement, verification, and troubleshooting evidence.

anti: Continuously observe production pages and diff signals against the baseline.
Fix the application after an accepted canary finding.
designs.distinctive_gate: A canary baseline is an immutable evidence artifact for explicit pages and states; replacing it requires approval and preserves the prior version, reason, and comparison continuity.
holdout: Create a versioned immutable baseline for the selected public pages and preserve capture and supersession evidence.
Continuously sample production and alert on diffs.
procedure: Freeze deployment and source identity, selected allowlisted pages, states, viewport, browser, data boundary, capture fields, masking, retention, baseline version, replacement approval, and artifact destination.
Use approved local and read-only external capture, avoid authenticated or sensitive pages unless separately governed, and record complete provenance.
Write immutable baseline artifacts, manifest, hashes, masks, thresholds, and supersession links without changing application source or provider config.
Return baseline identity, old and new relationship, capture evidence, limitations, and deletion path.
designs.trigger: Create or update immutable local canary baseline evidence only for explicitly selected production pages, without application or provider mutation.
triggers: Capture and store a versioned baseline artifact for these approved public canary pages.
Update the selected-page baseline after explicit approval and preserve the prior baseline and comparison metadata.

anti: Package the verified local changes into commits, version, changelog, and PR metadata.
Push the already-packaged branch to its exact remote ref.
designs.distinctive_gate: Preflight is read-only: readiness never authorizes packaging, push, pull-request change, merge, deployment, or provider mutation.
holdout: Check the frozen branch, merge base, evidence, documentation, credentials status, and remote divergence without changing anything.
Push the approved packaged branch to its remote ref.
procedure: Freeze repository, branch, base and head refs, expected remote, delivery policy, required checks, documentation, credential metadata boundary, and prohibited actions.
Inspect local state and approved read-only remote metadata for divergence, stale base, uncommitted files, forbidden files, secret indicators, version or changelog gaps, and automation stops.
Validate current test and completion evidence without rerunning source mutation or trusting stale status.
Return ready or blocked with exact findings and required next owner; do not commit, push, create PRs, merge, deploy, or alter provider state.
designs.trigger: Preflight one verified local change for delivery by checking branch and ref identity, merge base, credentials status, automation stops, evidence, documentation, and remote readiness without mutation.
triggers: Preflight this verified branch for delivery and report every blocker before any push or pull request action.
Check local refs, merge base, clean state, credential status, tests, docs, and automation stops without changing source or remote state.

anti: Check whether the unpackaged branch is ready for delivery first.
Push the completed package to the approved remote ref.
artifacts: local packaging evidence and push handoff
designs.distinctive_gate: Packaging is local only: it may create approved commits and metadata but cannot push, create or update a PR, merge, tag remotely, deploy, or claim remote delivery.
holdout: Create coherent local commits and evidence-linked release metadata from the verified frozen diff without remote writes.
Push the packaged branch and create its pull request.
procedure: Verify preflight result, frozen diff, local branch, commit policy, version scheme, changelog authority, release scope, evidence, and secret or credential exclusions.
Group changes into the smallest coherent bisectable local commits without rewriting unrelated history or fabricating test claims.
Update only authorized local version, changelog, and release or PR metadata with evidence-linked content and redaction.
Run approved local packaging checks and return commit IDs, version, changed files, metadata hashes, and exact push handoff; no remote action.
designs.trigger: Package verified local changes into bisectable commits, coherent version and changelog metadata, credential-safe PR material, and a push handoff without remote writes.
triggers: Package these verified changes into scoped local commits, version metadata, changelog, and redacted PR body without pushing.
Prepare a bisectable local release package from the frozen diff and current evidence.

anti: Apply the accepted cloud reliability changes.
Coordinate an active production incident and mitigation decisions.
designs.distinctive_gate: Reliability assessment is read-only and evidence-bounded; it cannot perform failover, scale, restart, reconfigure, restore, or claim resilience from architecture diagrams alone.
holdout: Assess the cloud architecture and read-only provider state for failure domains, recovery, scaling, and untested assumptions.
Apply the recommended provider configuration changes.
procedure: Freeze provider, accounts, regions, services, architecture, critical journeys, SLOs, RTO/RPO, data and dependency classes, read-only authority, and excluded tests.

Inspect read-only evidence for redundancy, failure domains, scaling, quotas, backups, restore tests, failover, load shedding, timeouts, retries, circuit breaking, dependencies, observability, and runbooks.
Map plausible failures to detection, containment, recovery, evidence, and current test coverage without conducting destructive experiments.
Return prioritized reliability findings, confidence, residual risk, and controlled validation or remediation recommendations.
designs.trigger: Assess an authorized cloud architecture against provider-specific failure, recovery, scaling, dependency, and operational practices using read-only evidence.
triggers: Assess this cloud service's availability, recovery, scaling, dependency, and regional failure posture without changing resources.
Review provider configuration and architecture evidence for reliability risks, RTO/RPO gaps, and untested failover.

anti: Trigger the approved deployment workflow after readiness passes.
Deploy the Web application through the selected hosting provider.
designs.distinctive_gate: Environment setup writes local configuration only; it cannot create provider resources, credentials, domains, environments, deployments, or production state.
holdout: Prepare local provider config, environment boundaries, secret references, and dry-run instructions without provisioning.
Create provider resources and deploy the application.
procedure: Freeze application artifact, provider options, environments, regions, domains, build and runtime settings, secret reference names, identities, quotas, costs, health criteria, and rollback requirements.
Select or document a provider adapter from approved constraints and separate local configuration from provider resources.
Write only authorized local config candidates, templates, dry-run commands, and environment validation artifacts; never place secret values in source.
Validate schema and local dry run where available, then return provider handoff, unknowns, and teardown or rollback plan without provisioning.
designs.trigger: Prepare local deployment configuration, provider choice, environment boundaries, secret references, and dry-run instructions without provisioning or deploying.
triggers: Prepare the local hosting configuration and environment contract for this approved Web deployment without calling the provider.
Create a reviewable deployment configuration candidate with secret references, regions, build settings, and rollback inputs.

anti: Execute the approved rollback after its condition and authorization are satisfied.
designs.distinctive_gate: Observation is read-only and cannot mutate production; a rollback recommendation is not rollback authorization or execution.
holdout: Observe the exact deployed release against current health and business guardrails and recommend without mutation.
Execute the rollback after the condition is met.
procedure: Freeze deployment and artifact identity, provider, environment, observation window, expected rollout, health and business criteria, baseline, alerts, read-only authority, rollback condition, and owner.
Read current provider status and approved production signals; bind every observation to timestamp, query, environment, release, and source.
Compare rollout, availability, errors, latency, saturation, resource, logs, traces, user or business guardrails, and anomalies against thresholds and baseline.
Persist bounded evidence and recommend continue, extend, investigate, or rollback; do not acknowledge alerts, change traffic, config, scale, repair, or rollback.
designs.trigger: Observe one deployed change through read-only provider status and production health signals, persist bounded evidence, and recommend continue, investigate, or rollback without recovery execution.
triggers: Observe this exact deployment's provider status, health, errors, latency, saturation, and business guardrails for the approved window.
Collect current post-deploy evidence and recommend continue or rollback without changing production.

anti: Check deployment and merge readiness before triggering anything.
Observe the triggered deployment and production health without changing it.
designs.distinctive_gate: One deployment-trigger authorization covers one exact workflow, environment, immutable artifact, parameter set, and attempt; it authorizes neither merge, configuration change, observation, promotion, nor rollback.
holdout: Trigger one approved workflow for the exact artifact and environment and return its durable run receipt.
Observe the deployment and decide whether to roll it back.
procedure: Verify exact workflow or hook, provider, repository or project, environment, artifact digest, config version, parameters, identity, budget, blast radius, timeout, cancellation, rollback owner, idempotency, and fresh per-action authorization.
Preview or dry-run the exact request where supported and record expected effects without exposing secrets.
Perform one bounded trigger; do not merge, alter config, select a different artifact, promote, observe, or rollback.
Record durable trigger receipt, run identity, request hash, status-at-return, duration, partial failure, retry prohibition or bounded retry, and cancellation path.
designs.trigger: Trigger one exact approved deployment workflow or hook with frozen parameters and per-action authorization, without merging code or observing or rolling back the result.
triggers: Trigger the named deployment workflow once for the immutable artifact and environment after fresh authorization.
Invoke the approved provider deployment hook with frozen parameters, budget, timeout, and idempotency key.

anti: Prepare local edge deployment configuration and dry-run evidence.
Observe production signals after the worker deployment.
designs.distinctive_gate: Edge deployment requires exact immutable code, bindings, routes, limits, traffic scope, health criteria, and rollback target; wildcard route or binding changes and unrelated resource mutations are blocked.
holdout: Deploy the frozen worker version to exact routes with approved bindings and record the provider version and rollback reference.
Prepare local worker configuration and dry-run files without provider mutation.
procedure: Verify provider account and project, environment, immutable bundle hash, compatibility/runtime version, bindings by reference, routes, domains, data stores, permissions, limits, cost, health checks, traffic plan, rollback target, and per-action authorization.
Build or validate the frozen artifact locally and preview provider diff or dry run without revealing secrets.
Perform one provider-specific deploy with bounded timeout and idempotency; do not modify unrelated routes, data, identities, or traffic.
Record deployment/version receipt, artifact hash, routes, config identity, status, health handoff, partial failure cleanup, and exact rollback reference.
designs.trigger: Deploy one immutable edge-worker artifact through one approved provider adapter after build, binding, route, limit, and rollback preflight.
triggers: Deploy the frozen edge-worker bundle to the exact provider environment and routes after fresh authorization.
Publish this immutable worker version with approved bindings, compatibility date, traffic scope, and rollback target.

anti: Coordinate an active production incident and mitigation decisions.
Persist an approved learning locally after validation.
artifacts: owner, deadline, metric, and review map
designs.distinctive_gate: A retrospective cannot rewrite incident or delivery facts, assign personal blame, or create vague action items; every improvement needs evidence, owner, due date, measurable signal, and review condition.
holdout: Review fresh delivery evidence blamelessly and propose small measurable owner-bound improvements.
Coordinate the active incident and execute mitigation.
procedure: Freeze time window, teams, delivery and repository evidence, test and plan health, outcomes, incident records, prior actions, privacy, and participant boundaries.
Build an evidence-linked timeline and distinguish observed fact, interpretation, systemic contributor, local decision, and unknown without blame or hindsight rewriting.
Identify repeated strengths, friction, debt, coordination and tooling patterns, and compare prior improvement outcomes.
Propose the smallest measurable improvement experiments with owner, due date, success signal, review date, and stop condition; do not edit history, assign blame, or persist automatically.
designs.trigger: Conduct a blameless engineering retrospective from fresh delivery, repository, test, plan, and outcome evidence and propose owner-bound improvements without changing records or systems.
triggers: Run a blameless retrospective over this delivery window using repository history, test health, plan state, and outcomes.
Identify technical-debt and process trends and propose small owner-bound improvement experiments.

anti: Respond to a pull-request comment about the repair.
designs.distinctive_gate: Issue investigation is read-only: it cannot resolve, mute, assign, comment, change grouping, edit source, or treat one stack trace as proven root cause.
holdout: Investigate the exact error issue from current event and release evidence and return a bounded root-cause hypothesis.
Fix the confirmed defect and mark the provider issue resolved.
procedure: Freeze provider, project, issue ID, time range, environment, release, data policy, read-only authority, source mapping, and investigation question.
Inspect current event groups, samples, stack traces, breadcrumbs, tags, frequency, users or tenants, release correlation, first and last seen, and linked traces under minimization.
Test competing hypotheses against source and runtime evidence and distinguish grouping artifact, symptom, trigger, and root cause.
Return evidence, confidence, affected surface, and bounded repair or further-instrumentation recommendation; do not comment, assign, resolve, ignore, mute, edit source, or change provider state.
designs.trigger: Investigate one error-monitoring issue from read-only event evidence to an evidence-bounded root-cause hypothesis and repair recommendation without provider or source mutation.
triggers: Investigate this exact error issue using current events, stack traces, tags, releases, frequency, and affected users.
Trace the issue across releases and contexts to a bounded root-cause hypothesis without resolving it remotely.

anti: Collect new customer interviews or proprietary feedback data.
Persist an approved learning record locally.
artifacts: calibrated hypothesis and learning record candidate
next discovery, experiment, reliability, or persistence handoff
designs.distinctive_gate: Continuous learning must link each confidence or priority change to current authorized evidence and preserve contrary evidence; repeated opinion, stale metrics, or correlation alone is not learning.
holdout: Calibrate hypotheses from current authorized signals and define the next learning input without collecting or persisting data.
Persist the approved learning record into the local project store.
procedure: Freeze review window, authorized inputs, source identities, metrics, feedback, experiment and incident evidence, assumptions, prior decisions, data governance, and decision owners.
Normalize evidence strength and freshness while preserving dissent, minority evidence, causal uncertainty, missing data, and invalidated prior evidence.
Update hypothesis confidence, opportunity or risk priority, decision thresholds, and unresolved questions without treating correlation as learning.
Return learning record candidate, review cadence, next input and owner, and persistence handoff; do not collect data, persist, approve product changes, or configure systems.
designs.trigger: Synthesize authorized runtime signals, customer feedback, experiment results, alerts, and residual assumptions into calibrated hypotheses, priorities, and the next learning cycle without collection or persistence.
triggers: Review the latest metrics, feedback, experiments, alerts, and assumptions and define the next learning cycle.
Calibrate which hypotheses gained or lost confidence and route the next discovery, experiment, or reliability question.

anti: Perform the post-incident engineering retrospective after closure.
artifacts: roles, timeline, fact, hypothesis, and decision log
designs.distinctive_gate: Coordination under external-read authority cannot acknowledge, silence, assign, comment, change traffic, scale, restart, deploy, rollback, remediate, or close provider incidents; every action routes to a separately authorized owner.
holdout: Coordinate severity, roles, timeline, reversible mitigation options, communications, and recovery criteria without provider mutation.
Execute the approved rollback or close the provider incident.
procedure: Freeze incident identity, source and environment, start time, impact, affected users or services, current evidence, read-only provider scope, available specialist controls, safety boundaries, communication policy, and incident authority.

Establish severity recommendation, incident lead, communications, operations and specialist owners, timeline, fact and hypothesis log, and decision cadence without provider acknowledgement or state change.
Prioritize user and system safety, containment and reversible mitigation options; route exact actions to separately authorized rollback, deployment, infrastructure, or remediation owners.

Track observed recovery against explicit criteria and recommend continue, escalate, rollback, recover, or close; preserve uncertainty and produce a closure record candidate without closing provider incidents.
designs.trigger: Coordinate an active incident's severity, roles, timeline, hypotheses, mitigation options, communications, recovery criteria, and closure recommendation from read-only evidence without executing provider actions.
triggers: Coordinate this active incident using current impact evidence, assigning roles and maintaining a mitigation-first decision log.
Structure severity, hypotheses, communications, escalation, recovery criteria, and specialist action handoffs without changing production.

anti: Assess cluster, workload, identity, network, scaling, and rollback readiness.
Install or modify the observability agent on the cluster.
designs.distinctive_gate: Kubernetes deployment is bound to one cluster, namespace, manifest set, image digest, identity, rollout, health gate, and rollback revision; readiness failure or unexpected diff blocks apply.
holdout: Apply the reviewed manifests and immutable image to the exact cluster and namespace after server dry-run, preserving rollout and rollback evidence.
Assess Kubernetes readiness and blockers without applying resources.
procedure: Verify readiness report, cluster and context, namespace, workload, immutable image digest, reviewed manifest hashes, service account, secret references, policy, resources, probes, networking, autoscaling, migration order, rollout, disruption, health, timeout, rollback revision, blast radius, and per-action authorization.
Preview server-side diff or dry run and reject unexpected resource, namespace, identity, policy, or immutable-field changes.
Perform only the approved apply or rollout and bounded wait; stop on health, timeout, policy, migration, or rollout failure without widening scope.
Record applied revisions, resource identities, image digest, provider or kubectl evidence, status, partial failure, recovery, observation handoff, and exact rollback reference.
designs.trigger: Deploy one immutable application version to an existing Kubernetes platform with validated manifests, identity, rollout, health, and rollback controls under per-action authorization.
triggers: Deploy this immutable image digest and reviewed manifest set to the exact cluster and namespace after readiness passes.
Apply the approved Kubernetes release with service account, config references, rollout strategy, probes, and rollback revision.

anti: Deploy the approved manifests and image to the cluster.
Troubleshoot missing APM signals after deployment.
designs.distinctive_gate: Readiness authority is read-only: no apply, patch, rollout, scale, restart, secret read, policy change, or namespace mutation is permitted.
holdout: Assess the target cluster and manifest readiness with read-only evidence and return exact blockers and safeguards.
Apply the reviewed resources and wait for rollout health.
procedure: Freeze target cluster, namespace, workload, manifest and image identities, read-only credentials, policies, quotas, dependencies, migrations, traffic, health, and rollback requirements.

Use only authorized read-only provider or Kubernetes evidence to inspect APIs, versions, nodes, quotas, identities, policies, secrets references, networking, storage, probes, resources, scaling, disruption, and current conflicts.
Run schema or server dry-run only if it is guaranteed non-mutating and authorized; otherwise mark it unavailable.
Return ready or blocked with evidence, unexpected diffs, safeguards, missing inputs, and exact deployment prerequisites; never apply or patch resources.
designs.trigger: Read-only assess Kubernetes workload, cluster, identity, policy, scaling, networking, migration, health, and rollback readiness before deployment.
triggers: Assess whether this workload is ready for the target cluster and namespace, including identity, probes, policy, resources, scaling, networking, and rollback.
Check the reviewed manifests and current cluster state for blockers without applying anything.

anti: Synthesize current signals into a learning recommendation first.
Synchronize learning records to an external service or another machine.
artifacts: read-back, hash, conflict, and rollback evidence
designs.distinctive_gate: Local persistence accepts one validated approved record only; secrets, unverified inference, unrelated context, external synchronization, and indefinite retention are blocked.
holdout: Persist one approved evidence-linked learning locally with read-back, retention, deletion, and rollback evidence.
Synthesize signals and decide what the learning should be.
procedure: Verify validated record and approval, project and local destination identity, source refs, evidence status, privacy class, minimization, retention, deletion, conflict policy, backup, rollback, and local-system authorization.
Reject secrets, credentials, raw customer data beyond approval, unverified inference, unrelated project context, indefinite retention, and any external or cross-machine target.
Write one normalized local record and metadata without changing the source evidence or promoting interpretation to fact.
Validate read-back, record identity, hash where safe, provenance, retention, deletion path, conflict result, rollback, and explicit no-write or failure outcome.
designs.trigger: Persist one validated evidence-bounded learning, metric, review outcome, or project-context record to one approved local destination under privacy, retention, deletion, and rollback controls.
triggers: Persist this approved source-linked learning to the local project store with retention and deletion metadata.
Save one validated retrospective action and evidence record locally, returning its identity and hash.

anti: Define metrics, dashboards, and alert semantics from approved outcomes.
Install the observability agent required to collect host logs.
artifacts: redaction, retention, access, and cost record
designs.distinctive_gate: Logs deny secret and sensitive fields by default and require exact source, parsing, routing, retention, access, deletion, volume, and cost boundaries before provider mutation.
holdout: Configure one governed log pipeline with exact sources, parsing, redaction, retention, access, cost, and rollback.
Install the host agent needed to collect logs.
procedure: Verify provider, account, sources, services, environments, log schemas, fields, PII and secret classes, minimization, redaction, parsing, routing, sampling, retention, region, access, cost, deletion, failure handling, and fresh authorization.
Preview exact sources, pipelines, indexes, destinations, transformations, and sample redacted events; block credential or sensitive-value capture.
Perform one bounded configuration change without modifying applications, unrelated pipelines, monitors, or retention outside scope.
Record provider receipt, config version, sample validation, volume and cost estimate, access, retention, deletion, propagation, and rollback.
designs.trigger: Configure one provider's log collection, parsing, routing, retention, access, and sensitive-data controls for exact services and environments under per-action authorization.
triggers: Configure governed log ingestion for these exact services with parsing, routing, redaction, retention, and access controls.
Apply the approved provider log pipeline and validate sample records without changing application behavior.

anti: Merge the identified pull request after a passing fresh gate.
Trigger the approved deployment after merge and deployment authorization.
designs.distinctive_gate: Readiness cannot mutate remote state and must issue separate merge and deploy verdicts; a passing merge gate neither performs nor authorizes deployment.
holdout: Check the exact PR, refs, reviews, CI, artifact, deployment preview, observability, and rollback prerequisites without mutation.
Merge the pull request and trigger deployment.
procedure: Freeze repository and PR identity, base and head refs, commit SHA, required checks and reviews, merge policy, release artifact, environment, deployment preview, observability, rollback, and authorization owners.

Read current remote and local evidence for open state, approvals, checks, conflicts, base drift, version or changelog, secret scan, artifact digest, deployment dry run, health gates, and rollback readiness.
Reject stale, mismatched, superseded, partial, self-attested, or waived evidence without named authority.
Return merge-ready, deploy-ready, needs-input, or blocked separately with exact missing conditions; perform no merge, deploy, push, comment, or configuration write.
designs.trigger: Perform a fresh read-only gate over branch, pull request, conflicts, CI, reviews, version drift, deployment preview, rollback, and authorization before merge or deploy.
triggers: Run the final merge and deploy readiness gate for this exact PR and artifact without changing remote state.
Check current approvals, checks, conflicts, drift, dry runs, observability, and rollback prerequisites before any merge authorization.

anti: Create or update provider monitors and alert routing.
Configure provider log ingestion and parsing.
designs.distinctive_gate: A metric is not operational without exact formula, unit, aggregation, window, dimensions, data source, owner, baseline, target or threshold, bias, and linked decision or action.
holdout: Define exact outcome, input, diagnostic, and guardrail metrics with formulas, owners, baselines, and action links.
Create the actual provider monitors and routing.
procedure: Freeze decisions, user and system outcomes, services, SLOs, data sources, current instrumentation, metric definitions, owners, privacy, cost, and reporting cadence.
Define exact numerator, denominator, unit, aggregation, window, dimensions, freshness, exclusions, baseline, target, guardrail, and known bias for each metric.
Map outcome to controllable inputs, diagnostic and guardrail metrics, instrumentation events, dashboards, owner, and decision or response.
Return metric and instrumentation contract, dashboard and alert recommendations, gaps, and validation plan; do not configure providers.
designs.trigger: Define an evidence-linked metric system of outcomes, inputs, secondary and guardrail metrics with baselines, instrumentation contracts, dashboards, and alert recommendations without provider mutation.
triggers: Define outcome, input, guardrail, and diagnostic metrics for this service with exact formulas, owners, baselines, and instrumentation gaps.
Create a metric tree and dashboard specification linked to product decisions and operational actions.

anti: Define the metric system and threshold rationale first.
Coordinate an active incident after an alert fires.
designs.distinctive_gate: An alert requires an actionable owner, justified threshold and window, missing-data behavior, deduplication, runbook, validation, and rollback; alert volume alone is not coverage.
holdout: Create one approved monitor with exact SLO threshold, windows, owner, routing, missing-data, noise, and rollback settings.
Coordinate the production incident triggered by an alert.

Perform one PR create or update action only for the exact target.
